A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Centaurus research work, including Appendices A–E. All 25 pages of each version are readable, and text, equations, figures, tables, and pseudocode can be matched across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original keyword-spotting, speech-denoising, and speech-recognition results in Section 5 and Appendix E, plus contraction-speed benchmarks in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the audio-task evaluations, architectural ablations, and Appendix C timing benchmarks.

M1.justification: The SSM block configurations, contraction-selection procedure, network architectures, objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SC35/SC10 keyword spotting, VoiceBank+DEMAND denoising evaluation, and LibriSpeech ASR evaluation. Appendix E also preserves the same DNS4-associated training sources and MLS English coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding experiments, including FRCRN and DeepFilterNet3 in Table 1, the ASR baselines in Table 2, and S4/S4D-Lin/LiquidS4/S5 in Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C and E retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, batch sizes, and timing-benchmark procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same connectivity and scaling ablations, real-versus-complex projection comparison, S6 state-size analysis, ASR module comparisons, and contraction-timing studies.

E5.justification: Figure 3 continues to specify ten training trials and median metrics. No repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, uncertainty-reporting practices, or statistical procedures change elsewhere.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. Examples include hybrid denoising PESQ 3.12 and 3.25 with causal convolution in Table 1, base ASR test WER 6.0/13.1 in Table 2, and SC10 accuracy 98.53 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, SSM generalization, Lemma 1 and its proof, canonical-form discussion, and contraction-cost derivations remain identical. Appendix A–B differences are page reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about flexible SSM connectivity, optimized tensor contractions, heterogeneous audio networks, and competitive fully state-space ASR.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the expressivity restriction from real projections, practical constraints on data gating, semi-manual contraction optimization, and explanations of unstable training.

D1.justification: The introduction and Reproducibility Statement replace the GitHub repository pointer with an OpenReview supplementary-material pointer for code access. Pseudocode, implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and data-processing instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. References that appear on different pages, including Zamba and Speech Commands, are retained rather than added or removed.

P1.justification: Two code-availability passages are briefly rewritten, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording, terminology, section order, and narrative structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised Reproducibility Statement causes minor reflow through the references and Appendices A–C, changing Listing 1's page split and Figure 4's vertical placement. Figure content, table designs, axes, legends, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, proofs, explanations, and detailed appendices are preserved. The revision redirects readers from GitHub to OpenReview supplementary material and introduces minor reflow. Both PDFs state code availability; neither establishes improved or worsened access, and the documented changes leave overall paper quality effectively unchanged.
